title: Unifying Isolated Spin-Down and Binary Recycling in Massive Neutron Star Formation via Relaxed Equation of State Axioms
abstract: The formation of massive neutron stars requires distinguishing isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down from binary recycling mechanisms. Current static equation of state axioms fail to unify these pathways for masses exceeding the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) limit. We relax the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state to formally incorporate the rotational and thermal support provided by binary mass accretion and companion ablation. This yields a unified pulsar evolution formal model and a novel mechanism-mass-spin relation. By mathematically verifying this framework, we establish the validity domain where massive neutron stars emerge from binary recycling rather than isolated collapse, resolving the mechanism explanation gap for dense matter equations of state.
core_contribution: Relaxing the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state to formally integrate the rotational and thermal support from binary recycling and companion ablation, yielding a unified mass-spin relation for massive neutron star formation.
method: 1. Assume relaxed_equation_of_state_axioms that relax standard stiffness constraints to permit >2.0 M_sun remnants via binary mass transfer. 2. Derive the mechanism_mass_spin_relation connecting isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down and binary recycling to observable spin periods and masses. 3. Construct the pulsar_evolution_formal_model unifying these pathways. 4. Verify the formation_evolution_verification by proving that the relaxed axioms consistently produce observed massive neutron star masses within the massive_neutron_star_validity_domain. 5. Perform a binary_recycling_mechanism_ablation to isolate the contribution of the relaxed axioms and confirm the resolution of the mechanism_explanation_gap.
risks: The primary risk is that the relaxed static equilibrium axioms may be mathematically equivalent to standard rotating neutron star models, offering no novel theoretical insight. Mitigation involves strictly bounding the validity domain to parameter spaces where the relaxed axioms provide a unified formalism not captured by standard perturbative rotating models.
rationale: This skill application resolves the mechanism explanation gap by explicitly identifying the candidate mechanism (binary recycling with relaxed EoS axioms) that explains massive neutron star masses. It sharpens the parent idea by replacing a weak assumption (standard EoS) with a refined one that formally unifies formation pathways.
